description:
Jologs or Jolog (Singular) is a subculture in the Philippines that emerged in the late 1990s to the late 2000s, with a colloquial term describing a rebellious, working-class subculture or an individual style often viewed by mainstream society as loud, tacky or lacking refinement. Similar to Olderbrothercore , the Mexican-American subculture Cholo , and Ah Beng from Singapore/Malaysia, its specific clothing type includes baggy streetwear, a bandana, sunglasses, headcaps, checkered polos, and a jersey tank top that is related to basketball and/or Hip-Hop .

It often centers on the prominence of pop culture phenomena perceived as mainstream or commercialized, which can incorporate music genres (such as New Wave/Synthpop, Hip-Hop, Post-Grunge and Rock/Metal), fashion, and any media that fit this aesthetic.
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Resilience, Rebellion, Self-Expression
